pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which faith honours the Bodhi tree most because of the Buddha? (1 mark)
   A. Islam
   B. Jainism
   C. Buddhism
   D. Sikhism

2. In the seed activity, why do we plant two tins? (1 mark)
   A. Because one tin is too small
   B. To make it look neat
   C. To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   D. To use up all the soil

3. The Beas river is linked with which region of India? (1 mark)
   A. Gujarat
   B. Punjab
   C. Bengal
   D. Kerala

4. Which of these is NOT one of the five elements? (1 mark)
   A. Vayu
   B. Metal
   C. Prithvi
   D. Agni

5. Which activity shows how to care for the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Burning waste in the field
   B. Planting a tree in the school compound
   C. Cutting trees for fun
   D. Throwing rubbish out of a matatu

6. Why is it a mistake to say there are four elements in the Panch Mahabhoot? (1 mark)
   A. There are five
   B. There are seven
   C. There is only one
   D. There are ten

7. What does maha mean in Mahabhoot? (1 mark)
   A. Small
   B. New
   C. Old
   D. Great

8. Which element is called Akash? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Water
   C. Space
   D. Fire

9. Which teaching is linked with Guru Ram Das Ji? (1 mark)
   A. Equality and serving others
   B. Pride
   C. War
   D. Wealth only

10. What does the word Guru mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A river
   C. A soldier
   D. A teacher who leads from darkness to light

11. Which city did Guru Ram Das Ji start? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Varanasi
   C. Mombasa
   D. Nairobi

12. What did Siddhartha later become? (1 mark)
   A. A Jain Tirthankar
   B. An Avtar of Vishnu
   C. The Buddha, the Awakened One
   D. A Sikh Guru

13. What rescue is Parshvanath known for in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. A snake in a burning log
   B. A drowning child
   C. A wounded swan
   D. A lost cow

14. What does Ahimsa mean? (1 mark)
   A. Not hurting any living being
   B. Paying taxes
   C. Telling stories
   D. Eating late

15. What was Guru Ram Das Ji's childhood name? (1 mark)
   A. Siddhartha
   B. Jetha
   C. Prahlad
   D. Ravi

16. Who was the king of Ayodhya in the Ramayan? (1 mark)
   A. Harishchandra
   B. Suddhodana
   C. Dasharatha
   D. Hiranyakashipu

17. Which of these were sons of King Dasharatha? (1 mark)
   A. Lakshman, Devadatta, Ram and Bharat
   B. Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   C. Ram, Sigala, Bharat and Shibi
   D. Prahlad, Ram and Jetha

18. What is a kaand in the Ramayan? (1 mark)
   A. A prayer
   B. A festival
   C. A river
   D. A section or book of the Ramayan

19. Which of the Sigalovada teachings shows how to treat the people who help us at home or work? (1 mark)
   A. Shout at them
   B. Respect and care for workers and helpers
   C. Pay no attention
   D. Ignore them

20. What does the langar teach? (1 mark)
   A. Greed
   B. Fear
   C. Pride
   D. Equality

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write three ways of conserving water in the community. (3 marks)

22. Match each element to its Sanskrit name: earth, fire, air. (3 marks)

23. Why is water sometimes used in worship? Give three points. (3 marks)

24. Explain how the school can plan a tree planting day that includes learners with special needs. (5 marks)

25. Describe Bharat's action after he returned to Ayodhya. (3 marks)

26. Name any four of the five great elements of the Panch Mahabhoot. (2 marks)

27. Tell the story of Prahlad and Hiranyakashipu in three sentences. (3 marks)

28. Give two lessons of the Bal Kaand. (2 marks)

29. Match each being with a teaching: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha, Guru Ram Das Ji. (4 marks)

30. Name the two Jain scriptures in this lesson. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Buddhism
   The Buddha became enlightened under a Bodhi tree.

2. C — To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   Comparing shows that water is needed for growth.

3. B — Punjab
   The Beas flows in Punjab, where Sikhism began.

4. B — Metal
   The five are earth, water, fire, air and space.

5. B — Planting a tree in the school compound
   Planting trees helps the environment.

6. A — There are five
   Panch means five.

7. D — Great
   Maha means great and bhoot means element.

8. C — Space
   Akash is the open sky or space that holds everything.

9. A — Equality and serving others
   He taught that all people are equal and service is important.

10. D — A teacher who leads from darkness to light
   A guru is a teacher and guide.

11. A — Amritsar
   The city that grew into Amritsar.

12. C — The Buddha, the Awakened One
   Siddhartha became the Buddha.

13. A — A snake in a burning log
   He asked the man to stop and the snake was saved.

14. A — Not hurting any living being
   Ahimsa is non-violence in thought, word and action.

15. B — Jetha
   His childhood name was Jetha.

16. C — Dasharatha
   King Dasharatha ruled Ayodhya.

17. B — Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   These were the four brothers.

18. D — A section or book of the Ramayan
   The Ramayan is divided into kaands.

19. B — Respect and care for workers and helpers
   Workers are one of the six directions.

20. D — Equality
   Everyone sits side by side to eat.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Closing taps, mending leaks, collecting rainwater, reusing water on plants, not polluting rivers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Earth: Prithvi. Fire: Agni. Air: Vayu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: It cleans, so it is a sign of purity; it is used to wash the hands and feet before prayer; it is poured or sprinkled to show a place is clean and ready.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a suitable place and get permission, prepare seedlings, tools and water, and give each child a job they can do, such as holding seedlings, filling watering cans or drawing the plants. Care for the trees afterwards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for permission, preparing, jobs for all, inclusion of special needs, and continued care.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: He refused the throne, went to ask Ram to return, took Ram's sandals and placed them on the throne, and ruled as a humble servant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: Prithvi (earth), Jal (water), Agni (fire), Vayu (air), Akash (space).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct element, up to 2 marks.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hiranyakashipu was a proud king who wanted to be called God. His young son Prahlad kept praying to Vishnu. Lord Narsimha appeared from a pillar and defeated the king.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the proud king, 1 mark for Prahlad's faith, 1 mark for Narsimha.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Respect for parents and teachers, love between brothers, courage to protect others, obedience to wise guidance (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each lesson.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha: God protects the good. Parshvanath: Ahimsa. Buddha: kindness to the hurt. Guru Ram Das Ji: honest work, equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct match.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kalpasutra and Uttaradhyayan Sutra.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
